subject: Building the estimation and prediction matrix

messages.author: 1c354fcf0a5dab6b
messages.subject: Building the estimation and prediction matrix
parts:
Hi there,

I'm trying to make some species distribution models, where the response variable (like presence or abundance of the species)  is linked to a set of environmental predictors.
Specifically, my data are point-referenced and thus I'm trying to fit this kind of model via the SPDE approach in R-INLA. 

Now I'm building both my estimation and prediction matrices according to Elias (http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/tutorials/spde/spde-tutorial.pdf), but I still have some doubt about these steps.
I will post some parts of my code for better understanding.

First I build my estimation matrix which contains some environmental predictors as follows:

# Estimation
N<-NROW(RESPONSE VARIABLE)
E<-data.frame(Intercept=rep(1,N),
                     Predictor1=pr1,
                     Predictor2=pr2,
                     Predcictor3=pr3)
                  
# Data stack for the observations       
stk.est<-inla.stack(data=list(y=RESPONSE VARIABLE),
                           A=list(A.est, 1),
                           effects=list(spatial=1:spde$n.spde,
                                        E),
                           tag="est")

The "A.est" is my estimation matrix related to my mesh and my observation points. My question is regarding the ''A'' argument in the inla.stack function. As you can see, I've specfied a list containing my estimation matrix and the number one.
Unfortunately I still can't understand very well for what this number stands for. Do I have to change this number according to the number of predictors specified in my data frame (in this case sould it equals to3)? 
This same question arises when I'm building my prediction stack.

My second question is how should I handle whith categorical predictors. I tried to fit my model containing one categorical predictor among a set of continuous predictor, but I always recieved the following notification after runing the model: 

"Error in inla(form1, family = "gamma", data = inla.stack.data(stk.est),  : With control.fixed = list(expand.factor.strategy='model.matrix'), then NA's in factor are not allowd. Please use strategy 'inla' instead."
In an earlier post I saw someone questioning the same thing...should I include  control.fixed = list(expand.factor.strategy='inla')  in my model specification?

Thank you in advance for any suggestion that would be very welcome.

Best regards,

Marie

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Building the estimation and prediction matrix
parts:
On 07/09/15 17:59, mach...@hotmail.com wrote:
Unfortunately I still can't understand very well for what this number stands for. Do I have to change this number according to the number of predictors specified in my data frame (in this case sould it equals to3)?

'A' and 'effects' are lists with same length. Each element in effect is related to each element in predictor, preserving the order. If your predictors are collected at the same set of location points, they should have the same projector matrix. Using 1 as a projector matrix means the same as Diagonal(n = length of the respective effect).
In an earlier post I saw someone questioning the same thing...should I include  control.fixed = list(expand.factor.strategy='inla')  in my model specification?

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Building the estimation and prediction matrix
parts:
The latent field is on a log scale. If you use "control.predictor =list(compute=TRUE, link =1)" in your inla call, the summary.fitted.values field will have the predicted mean on the natural scale. 

D
